lines.say: API stands for Application Programming Interface. Strip away the acronym, and it's a contract.
lines.cap: API: Application Programming Interface. Strip the acronym: a [contract].
lines.heard: API stands for Application Programming Interface. Strip away the acronym and it's a contract.

lines.say: One program asks another program to do something, without knowing how it gets done inside.
lines.cap: One program [asks] another to do something, without knowing [how].
lines.heard: One program asks another program to do something, without knowing how it gets done inside.

lines.say: The handbook's glossary puts it the same way: a defined contract, with no need to know the implementation.
lines.cap: The handbook glossary: a [defined contract], no need to know the [implementation].
lines.heard: The handbook's glossary puts it the same way. A defined contract with no need to know the implementation.

lines.say: Think of a wall socket. You plug in a lamp, and you know nothing about the power station.
lines.cap: Think of a wall [socket]. You know nothing about the power [station].
lines.heard: Think of a wall socket. You plug in a lamp and you know nothing about the power station.

lines.say: The shape of the socket is the promise.
lines.cap: The shape of the socket is the [promise].
lines.heard: The shape of the socket is the promise.

lines.say: Or think of a restaurant. You read the menu, you tell the waiter what you want, and the kitchen cooks it.
lines.cap: A restaurant: [menu], [waiter], [kitchen].
lines.heard: or think of a restaurant. You read the menu, you tell the waiter what you want and the kitchen cooks it.

lines.say: You never see the kitchen. It can swap chefs, change the stove, even rewrite the recipe.
lines.cap: The kitchen can swap [chefs], change the [stove], rewrite the [recipe].
lines.heard: You never see the kitchen. It can swap chefs, change the stove, even rewrite the recipe.

lines.say: As long as the dish matches the menu, you never notice.
lines.cap: As long as the dish matches the [menu], you never notice.
lines.heard: As long as the dish matches the menu, you never notice.

lines.say: That's the whole value of an API. Both sides can change independently, as long as the contract holds.
lines.cap: Both sides can [change independently], as long as the contract [holds].
lines.heard: That's the whole value of an API. Both sides can change independently, as long as the contract holds.

lines.say: This handbook focuses on web APIs. A client sends an HTTP request, and a server sends back a response.
lines.cap: Web APIs: a [client] sends a [request], a [server] sends a [response].
lines.heard: This handbook focuses on web APIs. A client sends an HTTP request and a server sends back a response.

lines.say: The client is anything that starts the conversation. A browser, a phone app, another service, a script.
lines.cap: The client is anything that [starts] the conversation.
lines.heard: The client is anything that starts the conversation. A browser, a phone app, another service, a script.

lines.say: M D N puts it plainly: the client always initiates. The server never does.
lines.cap: MDN: the client always [initiates]. The server never does.
lines.heard: MDN puts it plainly, the client always initiates, the server never does.

lines.say: Here's a real request. GET, slash users, slash forty-two.
lines.cap: A real request: [GET /users/42]
lines.heard: Here's a real request. Get slash users slash 42.

lines.say: GET is the method. It says what you want to do. The path says which thing you want.
lines.cap: The [method] says what to do. The [path] says which thing.
lines.heard: Get is the method. It says what you want to do. The path says which thing you want.

lines.say: Headers add context. Accept says you want JSON. Authorization says who you are.
lines.cap: [Headers] add context: what you accept, who you are.
lines.heard: Headers ad context, except says you want Jason, authorization says who you are.

lines.say: Every HTTP message, request or response, has the same shape: a start line, headers, an empty line, and an optional body.
lines.cap: Same shape: a [start line], [headers], an empty line, a [body].
lines.heard: Every HTTP message, request or response has the same shape. A start line headers an empty line in an optional body.

lines.say: The server answers with a status code. Two hundred means OK.
lines.cap: The server answers with a [status code]. [200] means OK.
lines.heard: The server answers with a status code. 200 means OK.

lines.say: Then comes the body, in JSON. An id, a name, an email.
lines.cap: Then the [body], in [JSON]: an id, a name, an email.
lines.heard: Then comes the body in J -SON, an ID and name and email.

lines.say: Nothing in this response says whether the data came from Post gress Q L, Mongo D B, or a plain dictionary. That's the point.
lines.cap: Nothing says if the data came from [PostgreSQL], [MongoDB] or a [dictionary].
lines.heard: Nothing in this response says whether the data came from PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or a plain dictionary. That's the point.

lines.say: Status codes come in families. Two hundreds mean success. Four hundreds mean the caller made a mistake. Five hundreds mean the server did.
lines.cap: [2xx] success. [4xx] the caller erred. [5xx] the server erred.
lines.heard: Status codes come in families. 200s mean success. 400s mean the caller made a mistake. 500s mean the server did.

lines.say: One more thing from M D N. HTTP is stateless. Every request stands alone, so the server doesn't remember the last one unless you send something that identifies you.
lines.cap: HTTP is [stateless]. Every request stands [alone].
lines.heard: One more thing from MDN. HTTP is stateless. Every request stands alone, so the server doesn't remember the last one unless you send something that identifies you.

lines.cap: Zoom out: the whole [trip], as a [sequence diagram].

lines.say: The client sends a request. The API matches the route and validates it.

lines.say: The client only ever depends on the API on the left. Everything to the right is free to change.

lines.say: Mistake one. Saying API when you mean REST API. APIs also include function signatures and operating system calls. REST is one architectural style for web APIs.
lines.cap: Mistake 1: API [is not] REST API.
lines.heard: Mistake 1. Saying API when you mean REST API. APIs also include function signatures and operating system calls. REST is one architectural style for web APIs.

lines.say: Mistake two. Copying your database columns straight into your responses. Rename a column, and every client breaks. Design the contract first, then the code behind it.
lines.cap: Mistake 2: mirroring your [database] in responses.
lines.heard: Mistake 2. Copying your database columns straight into your responses. Rename a column and every client breaks. Design the contract first, then the code behind it.

lines.say: Mistake three. Returning two hundred OK for everything, even errors. The status code is part of the contract. Use it.
lines.cap: Mistake 3: [200 OK] for everything, even errors.
lines.heard: Mistake 3, returning 200 OK for everything even errors. The status code is part of the contract. Use it.

lines.say: Mistake four. Confusing the API with the whole system, or with the user interface. A UI consumes an API. One API can serve a website and a mobile app.
lines.cap: Mistake 4: the API is not the [system] or the [UI].
lines.heard: Mistake 4. Confusing the API with the whole system or with the user interface. A UI consumes an API. One API can serve a website and a mobile app.

lines.say: And mistake five. Leaving the contract undocumented. If callers have to reverse engineer your behavior, it's not a contract. Part three of the handbook covers OpenAPI for exactly this.

lines.heard: and mistake five, leaving the contract undocumented. If callers have to reverse engineer your behavior, it's not a contract. Part three of the handbook covers open API for exactly this.
